sites.access: Free public stargazing every Friday night, year-round (weather permitting). Red-light-only campus: no white lights dusk–dawn.
sites.address: Ninigret Park, 62 Park Lane, Charlestown, RI 02813
sites.highlights: Guided observing with large telescopes; Milky Way plainly visible; special events for meteor showers and eclipses.
sites.name: Frosty Drew Observatory

sites.access: Night access via seasonal campgrounds (400+ sites; advance reservations). Day-use areas close at dusk.
sites.highlights: Big dark pine-barrens forest close to Boston; combine observing with an overnight camp.
sites.name: Myles Standish State Forest

sites.access: Seashore beaches, parking, and trails open 6 AM–midnight — fine for evening observing, not an all-night site. Seasonal beach fees may apply.
sites.highlights: Open ocean horizons in nearly every direction at the tip of the Cape; classic meteor-shower spot.
sites.name: Cape Cod National Seashore — Race Point

sites.access: Free parking at the trailhead. Organized night events have been held here; confirm after-dark access before visiting.
sites.highlights: Big open field shielded from headlights, in the dark-sky corridor of the Last Green Valley.
sites.name: Heins Farm Conservation Area (Sturbridge Trails)

sites.access: Public highway through White Mountain National Forest; overlook pullouts accessible at night. A day-use pass may be required for parking areas.
sites.highlights: Mountain pass at 2,855 ft with wide scenic overlooks (e.g., Pemigewasset Overlook); genuinely dark northern skies.
sites.name: Kancamagus Highway — Pemigewasset Overlook

sites.access: mass.gov lists hours as sunrise–sunset; night access is via wilderness camping only. Remote area — plan accordingly.
sites.address: 466 W. Hawley Road, Plainfield, MA 01070 (entrance on MA-8A, Hawley)
sites.highlights: One of the darkest accessible spots in Massachusetts; wilderness camping under the Milky Way.
sites.name: Kenneth Dubuque Memorial State Forest
